title: Best Dreo Dehumidifier (2026): 75, 95 & 110-Pint Compared
dek: Dreo brings its app-first approach to dehumidifiers. Here's which model to buy — and how to read those big pint numbers.
description: Which Dreo dehumidifier should you buy? We compare the 75, 95 and 110-pint smart models on real capacity, efficiency, drainage and app features.
intro: Best known for its fans and heaters, Dreo now sells a small lineup of smart dehumidifiers, and a **Dreo dehumidifier** has quickly become a common sight in Amazon results for basements and large rooms. All three current models connect to the Dreo app, drain by bucket or hose and promise quiet running. The catch is that their headline pint numbers come from three different sets of test conditions, which makes the lineup harder to compare than it looks.

We sorted it out by reading each listing's fine print, comparing the claims with ENERGY STAR and DOE norms, and weighing what matters day to day: drainage, controls, efficiency and warranty. Because Dreo doesn't sell a model with a built-in pump, we've also included two strong alternatives from other brands.
topPicksLead: The **Dreo 110-Pint Smart Dehumidifier** is the best Dreo for most homes: it has the largest tank, the most flexible modes and both Alexa and Google Home support.

products.name: Dreo 110-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (DR-HDH001S)
pros: Largest tank in the lineup at 2 gallons
Auto, Comfort and Continuous modes
Dreo app plus Alexa and Google Home
Dreo claims about 4.0 pints per kWh
Tip-over shutoff and ETL safety listing
cons: 110-pint figure is measured at 86°F and 90% humidity
Auto-defrost kicks in at 41°F, so it's not for cold crawl spaces
products.whyWeLoveIt: It's the most complete Dreo: the biggest tank, the widest choice of modes and the best smart-home support. In Auto mode you set a target and it varies fan speed to hold humidity within about 5 points, which is how a dehumidifier should behave in a living space.
products.performance: Dreo lists its capacity as 50 to 110 pints a day, with the top figure measured at 86°F and 90% humidity; the lower number is the one to compare with other brands' DOE ratings. It's rated for up to 4,500 square feet, and Dreo says the 2-gallon tank lasts more than 8 hours before it shuts off and lights a full-tank warning. A hose outlet handles continuous drainage, and the app adds schedules and real-time humidity readings.
products.notes: It comes in white or black. Sold under the listing name 711S on some pages; the model number on the label is DR-HDH001S.

products.name: Dreo 95-Pint ENERGY STAR Smart Dehumidifier (DR-HDH004S)
pros: ENERGY STAR certified, per Dreo
More capacity than the 75-pint under similar test conditions
App shows real-time energy use and cost
Dreo lists 41 dB operation
Child lock and timer
cons: 95-pint figure is measured at 95°F and 90% humidity
Smaller tank than the 110 for its capacity
products.whyWeLoveIt: If your basement gets genuinely wet in summer, this is the Dreo with the most muscle under hot, humid conditions. The energy monitor in the app is a useful bonus: it shows exactly what a long, damp season is costing you.
products.performance: Dreo's 95 pints come from a 95°F, 90% humidity test, so they're not comparable with DOE ratings, but they are comparable with the 75-pint's 95°F rating, which makes this the bigger machine. Dreo says it uses 49% less energy than standard DOE models. Its 1.85-gallon tank lasts up to about 10 hours, per Dreo, so plan on the hose in a wet basement.
products.notes: Oddly, the listing rates it for up to 3,000 sq ft while the smaller 75-pint claims 4,500. Size by dampness, using our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/), not by either figure.

products.name: Dreo 75-Pint ENERGY STAR Smart Dehumidifier (DR-HDH003S)
pros: ENERGY STAR certified, per Dreo
Dreo lists 41 dB operation
Dreo lists 30% less energy use than standard DOE models
App energy monitor, child lock and timer
cons: 75-pint figure is measured at 95°F and 95% humidity
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a muggy living room, home office or finished basement that's damp but not wet, the 75 is the most sensible Dreo. It shares the 95's quiet-running claim, soft display light and child lock, and Dreo says its tank lasts longer between emptyings — up to about 15 hours, versus about 10 for the 95.
products.performance: Dreo rates it at 75 pints a day at 95°F and 95% humidity and says it uses 30% less energy than standard DOE models. The child lock is handy in a family room, and the timer lets you run it during cheaper off-peak hours. Full-tank alerts, auto shut-off and auto-defrost round out the safety features.

products.whyWeLoveIt: If your basement has no floor drain below the unit, none of the Dreos can run unattended. This GoveeLife is the closest smart-home equivalent that can pump water up to a sink or out a window.
products.performance: Govee lists 50 pints a day at 65°F and 60% humidity, the same conditions as the DOE test, and coverage up to 4,500 square feet. That makes it easy to compare with DOE-rated models. Read more in our [best Govee dehumidifier](/best/best-govee-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Midea Cube 50-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (MAD50S1QWT)

products.whyWeLoveIt: If you'd rather buy on numbers you can check, the Cube 50 is the benchmark smart dehumidifier. Its ratings are listed in the ENERGY STAR database, and its oversized tank means far fewer trips to empty it.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR lists it at 49.67 pints a day, 2.01 liters per kWh and 515 kWh a year, and Midea rates it for up to 4,500 square feet. The humidistat adjusts from 35% to 85%, and a gravity hose handles continuous drainage. See the whole range in our [best Midea dehumidifier](/best/best-midea-dehumidifier/) guide.

sections.heading: How we pick the best Dreo dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. For a newer brand like Dreo, we read each listing's specifications closely, note the temperature and humidity behind every capacity claim, compare efficiency claims with ENERGY STAR and DOE norms, and read owner reviews for recurring issues such as app pairing trouble, sensor accuracy and drainage leaks. We also check CPSC recall records.

We ranked the lineup on what you'll live with every day: how precisely each model holds a setpoint, how long it runs between emptyings, how well it drains continuously, and how much of its marketing you can verify.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Dreo dehumidifier

items.label: Compare pints at the same conditions
items.text: A pint figure means nothing without its test temperature. The 75 and 95 were both rated at 95°F; the 110's top figure was rated at 86°F.

items.label: Drainage plan
items.text: All three take a hose. If your drain is higher than the unit, you need a pump model from another brand; see our [dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) picks.

items.label: Voice control
items.text: Only the 110-Pint's listing mentions Alexa and Google Home. The 75 and 95 focus on the Dreo app.

items.label: Temperature
items.text: Like most household units, Dreos defrost in cool air. Keep them in spaces that stay above the low 60s for full output.

items.label: Warranty
items.text: Dreo lists 12 months on the 75 and 95, about the same as Midea's coverage.

sections.heading: How to read Dreo's pint ratings

blocks.text: Since 2019, the U.S. Department of Energy has rated dehumidifiers in a 65°F room at 60% humidity — conditions much like a real basement. Hot, saturated air gives up far more water, so the same machine can be quoted at 50 pints under the DOE test and more than 100 pints at 95°F. That's why Dreo's numbers look so much bigger than Midea's or Frigidaire's.

The best clue in Dreo's lineup is the 110-Pint's own range: "50 to 110 pints." The low end is the figure to compare with DOE-rated 50-pint units. For the 75 and 95, Dreo doesn't give a DOE number, so treat them as large-basement-class machines and size by dampness. Our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) explains the rating change in detail.

sections.heading: Dreo dehumidifier setup, manual and troubleshooting

blocks.text: Most app-pairing problems with smart appliances come down to the network: many only join 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, so if your router combines bands under one name, temporarily separate them during setup. Stand near the unit, keep Bluetooth on and follow the app's steps. Our [Wi-Fi dehumidifier](/best/best-wifi-dehumidifier/) guide explains what an app can and can't do.

Attach the included hose, run it downhill to a floor drain without kinks or rises, and keep the hose end below the outlet. A full-tank light with the hose attached usually means the hose isn't seated or has a high spot.

Rinse the intake filter every few weeks in season and let it dry fully before reinstalling. A clogged filter cuts airflow, raises energy use and can trigger frosting. Our [dehumidifier maintenance](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) guide has a full checklist.

Find the model number on the rating label — DR-HDH001S, DR-HDH003S or DR-HDH004S — and search it on Dreo's support site or in the app. If the unit keeps freezing or stops collecting water, our [not collecting water](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/) guide covers the usual causes.

For most buyers, the **Dreo 110-Pint** is the Dreo to get: the biggest tank, true Auto mode and the best smart-home support. Choose the **Dreo 95-Pint** for a wet basement with a floor drain, or the **Dreo 75-Pint** for a muggy living space. If your drain is above the unit, skip Dreo for the **GoveeLife with Pump**, and if you want verified DOE numbers, the **Midea Cube 50** remains the benchmark.

faqs.a: They're well-featured smart dehumidifiers with app control, hose drainage and, on the 75 and 95, ENERGY STAR certification per Dreo. The main caveat is that their headline pint figures are measured at hot, humid conditions, so compare them carefully with DOE-rated models.

faqs.q: Is the Dreo 110-pint dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: Yes, if you want the most complete Dreo. It has a 2-gallon tank, Auto, Comfort and Continuous modes, and Alexa and Google Home support. Its 110-pint figure is measured at 86°F and 90% humidity; Dreo's own range starts at 50 pints.

faqs.q: Does the Dreo dehumidifier have a pump?
faqs.a: None of the three current models lists a built-in pump. They drain into a tank or through a gravity hose. If your drain is above the unit, choose a pump model such as the GoveeLife with Pump.

faqs.q: Does Dreo work with Alexa and Google Home?
faqs.a: The 110-Pint's listing includes Alexa and Google Home voice control. The 75 and 95 are controlled through the Dreo app.

faqs.q: What size Dreo dehumidifier do I need?
faqs.a: For a damp but not wet basement or a muggy living space, the 75-Pint. For a wet basement or the most flexible features, the 95 or 110. Size by how damp the space is rather than by the listed square footage.

faqs.q: Where can I find the Dreo dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: Look up the model number on the unit's rating label (DR-HDH001S, DR-HDH003S or DR-HDH004S) on Dreo's support site or in the Dreo app.
